newsitem.title: THAILAND: Short-term increase in Thai rate possible-Seamico.
newsitem.headline: Short-term increase in Thai rate possible-Seamico.

text.p: Seamico Research said on Monday that a short-term increase in Thai commercial banks' interest rates was possible during the first quarter of 1997 if the central bank failed to manage money market liquidity.
Seamico said in a research report that medium-term outlook for interest rates continued to be a declining trend, with a maximum decline of one percentage point seen for 1997.

"The M2 is declining, primarily due to slow deposit growth, so money market liquidity should remain tight. The BOT (Bank of Thailand) has intervened, however, thus easing the tight liquidity," it said.
The report said the situation depended on how well the central bank could manage liquidity and another hike in interest rates was likely if it failed.

Two major commercial banks including Bangkok Bank Plc and Thai Farmers Bank Plc cut their 3-month fixed-deposit rates by 25 basis points recently while two other banks -- Krung Thai Bank Plc and Siam Commercial Bank Plc -- were likely to follow, it said.
A decline in deposit rates would result in a further slowing of deposit growth, it said.
Deposit growth tumbled to 12.9 percent year-on-year in October from 23.3 percent year-on-year in March, primarily due to strong cuts in deposit rates during the first half of 1996.
"This will put more pressure on banks to mobilise more deposits in order to extend more loans, so deposit rates will be on the rise in Q1 97," it said.
Seamico said the key to surviving next year would be how well the policy makers can restore Thailand's economic confidence.
"An improvement in economic figures would give a strong boost to investor confidence and would boost liquidity in turn," it said. "But we do not expect to see this before H2 97," the report added.
